newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila T-bill market lacklustre amid uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Manila T-bill market lacklustre amid uncertainty.

text.p: Lack of buying appetite marked Tuesday's secondary market trading in Treasury bills as banks continued to be wary amid the currency woes in the region, traders said.
"Banks are giving higher bid and offer rates. But in terms of actual buying and selling, there's not much," a trader said.
"It's hard to go to Treasury bills when the overnight borrowing rate is at 22 percent," another said.
"There's still a lot of uncertainty. There's a lot of real demand for dollars," she added.
Traders said attention was on bidding for the 35-day and 42-day bills in the auction later.
"It's better to go to the auction and later make a trading gain. It's easier to sell short-term bills," a foreign bank trader said.
The average interbank call loan rate fell to 22.03125 percent from 25.03125 percent in line with the three percentage-point cut in the central bank's overnight borrowing rate to 22 percent.
Out of the 38 participating financial institutions, 24 were lenders. Volume was higher at 12.41 billion pesos from 11.04 billion. -- Lilian Karunungan (63 2) 841-8937
